assets.label: ILLUSTRATION · NOT INCIDENT EVIDENCE

scenes.label: 01 / OPEN WITH THE EVIDENCE
scenes.headline:
Start with
what we can see.
scenes.body: A short source clip can introduce the question. This illustration is a synthetic example.
scenes.footnote: Template demonstration · not a real event

scenes.label: 02 / KEEP THE CONTEXT
scenes.headline:
Several posts.
How many cases?
scenes.body: Match reposts to their original incident before presenting them as separate reports.

scenes.label: 03 / EXPLAIN THE DETAIL
scenes.headline:
Let the close-up
add information.
scenes.body: Use the source to identify the relevant detail. Preserve context in both crops.

scenes.label: 04 / MAKE IT UNDERSTANDABLE
scenes.headline:
Collect. Check.
Then explain.
scenes.body: Use a few simple steps to explain the finding without adding unsupported detail.

scenes.label: 05 / ATTRIBUTE THE RESPONSE
scenes.headline:
Give the source
a clear voice.
scenes.body: Distinguish a direct quotation from an editorial summary, and retain the speaker's scope.
scenes.quote: An attributed account still needs context.
scenes.attribution: Synthetic layout example · not a real quotation

scenes.label: 06 / KEEP THE LIMITS VISIBLE
scenes.headline:
Say what
remains unknown.
scenes.body: A useful report makes the unresolved questions as clear as the established findings.

scenes.label: FOLLOW THE SOURCES
scenes.headline:
One story.
A traceable record.
scenes.body: Link the originals, preserve the research date, and keep the accompanying post aligned.
scenes.footnote: Synthetic demonstration · replace with your researched episode
